newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan, Iran vow to cooperate against enemies.
newsitem.headline: Sudan, Iran vow to cooperate against enemies.

text.p: Sudan and Iran vowed on Monday to strengthen ties in the face of "enemy forces" which they said were trying to stir up trouble between Islamic countries.

In a joint statement issued at the end of a visit by Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, the two countries criticised double standards they said Western countries used at the United Nations to impose their values and culture on the Moslem world.
Rafsanjani arrived in Sudan on Sunday on a six-nation African tour.

"The two sides studied the current circumstances in the Islamic world in the light of attempts by enemy forces to sow differences between Moslem countries and people and stressed the need to cooperate and coordinate efforts to follow policies that will preserve unity among Moslem societies," the statement said.
Sudan's Arab neighbours say Khartoum's Islamist-backed government has been a conduit for bringing Iran's brand of revolutionary Islam into the region.
"The two sides rejected the double standard that is followed by some in international organisations and through agencies of the United Nations and that is aimed at independent countries.

"It is intended to impose values and cultures in a way that threatens such independence and negates the will and right to choose the system of rule that is appropriate to their own values and culture," it added.
Sudan and Iran also called for an "independent Palestinian state," saying Palestinians had the right to "a just holy struggle and the right to get back their occupied land".
The two countries also supported each other's policies. Iran said the civil war in southern Sudan was an internal matter to be solved according to Sudanese law.
Sudan praised Iran's "active and positive role in spreading peace and stability in its region" and echoed Tehran's call for the departure of foreign troops from the Gulf.
Khartoum also thanked Iran for mediating in its conflicts with its African neighbours. Rafsanjani persuaded Sudan and Uganda to reestablish ties after a 16-month break.
